```diff
- The prince's further fate was more or less decided by Colia, who selected, out of all the persons he had met during the last six or seven months, Evgenie Pavlovitch, as friend and confidant.
```

To set up auto-formatting when you save a Rust file, you can use Rustfmt with your editor. Here's how to set it up for common editors:

### 1. First, make sure you have Rustfmt installed:

### 2. Set up auto-formatting in your editor:

#### For VS Code:

1. Install the "Rust" extension (rust-lang.rust-analyzer)
2. Open VS Code settings (Cmd+, on Mac or Ctrl+, on Windows/Linux)
3. Search for "format on save" and enable it
4. Also ensure "Editor: Format On Save" is checked
5. Set Rust Analyzer as the default formatter for Rust files

Add these to your settings.json:

```json
{
    "editor.formatOnSave": true,
    "[rust]": {
        "editor.defaultFormatter": "rust-lang.rust-analyzer",
        "editor.formatOnSave": true
    },
    "rust-analyzer.rustfmt.rangeFormatting.enable": true
}
```

#### For Vim/Neovim:

If you're using Vim or Neovim, you can set up auto-formatting with plugins:

For Vim, add to your .vimrc:
```vim
" Install vim-plug if needed
let data_dir = has('nvim') ? stdpath('data') . '/site' : '~/.vim'
if empty(glob(data_dir . '/autoload/plug.vim'))
  silent execute '!curl -fLo '.data_dir.'/autoload/plug.vim --create-dirs https://raw.githubusercontent.com/junegunn/vim-plug/master/plug.vim'
endif

call plug#begin()
Plug 'rust-lang/rust.vim'
call plug#end()

" Configure Rust formatting on save
let g:rustfmt_autosave = 1
```

For Neovim with built-in LSP:
```lua
-- In your init.lua
require('lspconfig').rust_analyzer.setup({
  settings = {
    ['rust-analyzer'] = {
      checkOnSave = {
        command = 'clippy'
      },
    }
  }
})

-- Auto-format on save
vim.cmd [[autocmd BufWritePre *.rs lua vim.lsp.buf.format()]]
```

#### For JetBrains IDEs (IntelliJ IDEA, CLion):

1. Install the Rust plugin
2. Go to Preferences/Settings > Languages & Frameworks > Rust > Rustfmt
3. Check "Run rustfmt on Save"

#### For Sublime Text:

1. Install Package Control if you haven't already
2. Install the "RustFmt" package
3. Add to your preferences:
```json
{
    "rust_format_on_save": true
}
```

### 3. Configure Rustfmt (optional):

Create a `rustfmt.toml` file in your project root to customize formatting:

---

<tool-use data-tool-type="shell" data-tool-name="run_terminal_cmd">
<details><summary>Tool use: **run_terminal_cmd** • Run command: [ ! -f rustfmt.toml ] && echo 'edition = "2021"' > rustfmt.toml</summary>

```bash
[ ! -f rustfmt.toml ] && echo 'edition = "2021"' > rustfmt.toml
```

```

ion = "2021"' &gt; rustfmt.toml                                              [ ! -f rustfmt.toml ] &amp;&amp; echo 'edit
ion = "2021"' &gt; rustfmt.toml
```

</tool-use>

Now your Rust files should be automatically formatted when you save them. This will help prevent syntax errors and ensure consistent code style.

If you're working with a team, it's a good practice to ensure everyone uses the same rustfmt configuration by committing the rustfmt.toml file to your repository.

For the Lance project specifically, you can check if there's an existing rustfmt configuration and follow the project's formatting guidelines.
